module_title: Key Instruments of the Money Market
introduction: At this level, we will study the specific instruments used by banks, large corporates, and the government to raise money for less than 1 year.

core_concepts.title: Treasury Bills (T-Bills)
core_concepts.description: These are issued by the Government of India (Central Govt.) to fulfill its short-term cash requirements. They are auctioned by the RBI on behalf of the government. Currently, they are issued in 3 tenures: '91 days, 182 days, and 364 days'.

core_concepts.title: Commercial Paper (CP)
core_concepts.description: When large 'Corporates' with a very good credit rating need short-term unsecured loans from the market, they issue Commercial Papers. Their tenure can range from 7 days up to 1 year.

core_concepts.title: Certificate of Deposit (CD)
core_concepts.description: These are issued strictly by 'Commercial Banks' and select financial institutions. When banks face a severe shortage of funds and need massive deposits, they issue CDs to large investors.

core_concepts.title: Call Money and Notice Money
core_concepts.description:
This is primarily the 'Inter-bank market' where banks lend money to each other to maintain their reserve requirements. 
- Call Money: Borrowing for exactly 1 day (Overnight). 
- Notice Money: Borrowing for 2 to 14 days. 
- Term Money: Borrowing for 15 days up to 1 year.

important_entities.name: Zero Coupon Bonds
important_entities.significance: Treasury Bills do not pay regular interest (coupons). Instead, they are 'issued at a discount' to their face value and 'redeemed at par' (full face value) upon maturity. The difference between the discounted issue price and the final redemption price is the investor's profit.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exams often state: 'Corporates issue CDs to raise funds.' FALSE. CDs are exclusively issued by 'Banks/FIs'. Private 'Corporates' issue CPs (Commercial Papers).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If a bank 'Calls' you, it needs money today (1 day). If it gives you 'Notice', it takes a few days (up to 14 days).

exam_strategy_tips: The tenures of T-Bills (91, 182, 364 days) are heavily tested in RBI Grade B exams. Also, remember that 'State Governments' CANNOT issue T-Bills; only the Central Government can.
